forcedChoices.choice: pueda decirles: “Amigo mío, ¿por qué te sientas…?”
forcedChoices.reason: Jesus speaks to a group (ustedes); the host's words inside go to one guest (tú).
Each guest answers one servant; Spanish needs tú or usted, and a guest to a servant takes tú.
Jesus addresses the one messenger, so tú.
The apostles speak to the Master as a close associate, as elsewhere in these papers.
Masculine pronoun points to the apostles, whom the context shows Jesus rebuked; Spanish gender forces the choice that the English 'them' leaves to context.
